questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go out and experience the nature in Norway and gain an international network.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Really easy, both KU and UiB had really good information on their webpages.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: All the necessary. We had two information meetings in the beginning, which was really nice. We also had one week of introduction, where you are put into different groups, so you meet a lot of other international students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Quite easy. I used a page called
Hybel.no
, where you can find private housing. I lived in an apartment with six other people, which was perfect for me. I had my own room and then we shared the kitchen and two bathrooms.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to first apply for the SAMMEN housing options in the city center. If you don't get anything, then apply for privat housing. Here I would also recommend to live in or close to the city center. I lived behind "Bryggen" and that was good. I know a lot of people living at fantoft, but it takes 25 minutes to the city center. So I chose not to live there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's really easy to find the courses and UiB send you a whole guide to register for courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get a link for the page called "Studentweb" where you can register for the courses. Here you get a whole list of all the course options.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help from the student administration, student center, faculty coordinators, etc.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Really succesfull, I got all the courses that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to look at the exam date for all the courses, they might overlap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I'm at my master program in Economics, and there were not a lot of master courses. So I took two bachelor courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was the same as in Denmark I would say. Not more difficult, but not easier.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty much the same. Both lectures and exercise classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Advanced mathematics and optimization, Investment and financing, Strategic Behaviour and Markets Power

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Strategic Behaviour and Markets Power, but it's in norwegian.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Flight tickets for going home to Denmark.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and alcohol in Norway are more expensive than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are a lot of bars and clubs in Bergen. The going-out life is really nice and they party both thursday, friday and saturday.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of sport clubs, social activities, hiking with SAMMEN, trips with ESN Bergen, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go hiking on the seven mountains.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Use the time to go on trips. I went to Stavanger, Tromsø, Oslo, Geilo and two times on a cabin trip.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy, it's not that different from the culture in Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and take initiative, because Norwegians are not the most open people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Drinking alcohol in public is not allowed in Norway, so in the summer, it was a shame that we couldn't sit in a park and drink.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The norwegian culture and nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open and ready to spend a lot of time outdoors. It rains a lot in Bergen, so be prepared to find activities to do when the weather is bad.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember warm clothes, rain gear and hiking boots.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I have made new friends from different countries, with whom I have become very close. We got a very special bond with each other, which is unique.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: For me, exchange was generally a challenge. I have really stepped out of my comfort zone, which I am incredibly happy about now and I am very proud of myself. So if you're considering an exchange, go and go to Bergen. It's such a great study city.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
